items.title: Public Meetings to Consider Zoning Amendments
RZ003-2025 - 7735 Sixth Line, Nichol
notes: Mayor Watters indicated the purpose of this public meeting is to present and receive public input regarding a proposed zoning by-law amendment on the subject land known as 7735 Sixth Line in the former Township of Nichol.

He noted the purpose of the proposed zoning by-law amendment is to change the zoning from “A” Agricultural and “EP” Environment Protection to “A” Agricultural Exception and “EP” Environment Protection on the retained parcel to restrict residential uses.

The effect of the proposed zoning by-law amendment is to implement zoning regulations necessary to facilitate a surplus farm dwelling severance. The zoning amendment is a condition of approval of the County of Wellington Land Division Committee Application B108-24.

Mayor Watters indicated if a person or public body would otherwise have an ability to appeal the decision of the Township of Centre Wellington to the Ontario Land Tribunal (OLT) but the person or public body does not make oral submissions at a public meeting or make written submissions to the Township of Centre Wellington before the by- law is passed, the person or public body is not entitled to appeal the decision.

Mayor Watters stated if a person or public body does not make oral submission at the public meeting, or make written submissions to the Township of Centre Wellington before the by-law is passed, the person or public body may not be added as the party to the hearing of an appeal before the OLT unless, in the opinion of the Tribunal, there are reasonable grounds to do so.

Mayor Watters advised if anyone wishes to be notified of the adoption of the proposed zoning by-law amendment, a written request must be filed with the Municipal Clerk, Township of Centre Wellington, 1 MacDonald Square, Elora, ON, N0B 1S0.

The Municipal Clerk advised notice was mailed to prescribed persons, agencies and public bodies on or before April 17, 2025. She indicated a copy of the notice was advertised in the Wellington Advertiser on April 17, 2025 and confirmed the requirement for giving notice was completed on April 17, 2025.
Mayor Watters called on Deanna Maiden, Senior Development Planner, to introduce the application, indicating the application is to prohibit residential uses to facilitate a farm surplus dwelling.
Mayor Watters called on Hailey Keast, Planning Technician from Van Harten Surveying to provide an overview of the application.
Mayor Watters indicated no delegations have registered and asked if there is anyone present wishing to speak to the application.
There being none, Mayor Watters offered Council an opportunity to ask questions of the applicant or staff.
There being no questions, Mayor Watters thanked everyone for attending and advised Council will be considering the by-law at a future Council meeting.
Mayor Watters declared the public meeting adjourned.

items.title: Engagement Strategy Introduction
notes: Report from Kendra Martin, Manager of Strategic Initiatives and Communications

Kendra Martin, Manager of Strategic Initiatives and Communications introduced Tannis Topolnisky, Topent Ltd. T. Toplnisky provided a project update, noting the overall project goals, the deliverables, the timelines, engagement ideas and the expectations of success.

items.title: Parks and Recreation Plan Draft Report
notes: Report from Pat Newson, Managing Director of Community Services Pat Newson, Managing Director of Community Services introduced consultants Tracey McQueen and Jennifer Reynolds, MGA Group, and Terry Alyman, Steve Wever and Michael Witmer from GSP Group. T McQueen outlined the four ongoing projects; a) Needs Assessment, b) Parks Plan, c) Parks and Recreation Plan and d) Feasibility Study. She outlined the project journey from the initial research phase to the deliverables.

T. McQueen outlined the next steps in the process, including posting the plans on Connect CW and continuing to receive feedback from members of Council and the advisory committees. She noted the plan to return to Council at the July 14th meeting to share the feedback received and report on any refinements to the plans and seek final adoption.

Staff and the consultants responded to questions regarding appropriate service standards for parkland, renewal of existing parks, and plans to incorporate park amenities at the new Operations Centre such as walking tracks and picnics.
Mayor Watters called for a 10 minute recess, the meeting resumed at 3:36 pm.
